# Spiritual Translation of the Chapter

---

** ¶1. ** There are those among us who say that the Divine wills the existence of the external natural human. They reason thus : The proce eding Divine Wisdom projected the form of its own order into the natural mind, and the self -derived faculties of that mind — its ruling loves and governing powers — perceived this form and shaped the external human after its likeness, which are the will and the understanding in their merely natural state . See , then, they say, the Divine cons ents to this , for it has made its order visible to the self -derived faculties, and they have constructed accordingly . Had the Divine not willed the natural human , it would never have unc overed its form, nor would the self-derived powers have fashioned human nature after its likeness.

---

**¶2.** But regarding the proce eding Divine Wisdom: when it descended and made itself perceptible in the natural mind , it did not come in order to reveal its form to the self -derived faculties of that mind. Rather, it came and made itself manifest because of the interior spiritual life and the interior divine truth — its own ind welling good — which was dispers ed throughout every state , that it might restore it to life and accomplish its liberation , and free what is spiritual from every bond of falsity and every f etter of evil desire in which it was entangled and held capt ive.

---

**¶ 3.** Still , consider this: the self -derived faculties and governing powers of the natural mind, having no genuine form of their own, coveted the form of Divine Wisdom when they perceived it. They reflected upon themselves and recognized that nothing in their own creation resembled it . They im printed this perceived form upon their will and upon their understanding. Afterward they constructed the external human after its likeness — the natural will and natural understanding. They sealed the image of the Divine within themselves . And so they produced an imitation; but they did not reproduce it in truth. For what they fash ioned came from themselves , and though it out wardly resembles the Divine order , it does not in wardly correspond to it. So too is the external form of the natural human: it was copied against the pattern of the Divine, but it is not that pattern in reality .

---

**¶4 .** Similarly with perception itself — for while it outwardly resembles genuine spiritual perception, it has not been repro duced in truth.

---

**¶5. ** This matter may be understood through the following lik eness: There is a pure and noble wisdom, free in its origin , dwelling within the inmost states of heaven, rich in all spiritual goods and poss essions, beautiful in the radiance of its truth, and virt uous in its holiness. It moves in a free and ex alted state . The fame of its beauty has spread through every province of the mind, sur passing all else . Within its inmost chamber, the n oblest aff ections and the highest loves desire to behold its beauty. Yet they cannot reach it, for it remains hidden within its celest ial dwelling . Now this pure wisdom does not come forth from its inmost state into the external world of its own accord or for the sake of display . But when its beloved — the interior good that is its own life — is in suffering, then this wisdom leaves its in most chamber and comes into the open , into the midst of all states of mind , and reveals its face and its beauty, solely because of its beloved . This wisdom , upon which no merely natural faculty had ever looked, and whose inner quality no one had ever perceived , neither des iring nor del ighting in out ward display — it leaves its interior state behind and comes into the midst of the human mind so that all may be hold it: the noble aff ections and the honor able thoughts , and even the lowest servants of the natural mind, all look upon it.

---

** ¶6.** In accordance with this lik eness: this too is how the proceeding Divine Wisdom acts . As this pure wisdom does not come forth in w antonness or pride, nor does it consent to the outer world for the outer world's sake, it reveals its form and its beauty only under the compulsion of grief and love for what is beloved and suffering within.

---

** ¶7.** This, then, is the way of the proceeding Divine Truth in its third operation : when it descended and displayed the form of divine order before all the powers of the natural mind. It did not come so that all the self -derived fac ulties and governing authorities would sculpt an external form after its likeness. Rather, it came because its own interior truth was crucified — that is, dispersed and suffering throughout every level of the natural mind — so that it might release that truth, free it, and rescue it from opp ression. Yet when the self -derived faculties beheld this form , they coveted its beauty. They fashioned the natural will and natural understanding — the external human — after its likeness, without the consent of the Divine itself .

---

**¶9 .** Understand also this further teaching : Just as the natural will and understanding were fashioned by the self-derived faculties and stam ped after the form of the Divine, so too a mult itude of intermediate spiritual powers and angelic intellig ences received the im press of that form when it was displayed to them. For in the majesty of its wisdom and the warmth of its love, they burned with lon ging and were und one by their own desire — like one who ga zes upon a beauty beyond compreh ension and is consumed by the force of that desire .

---

**¶10 .** This is also the case with those powers: when they beheld that majestic and beautiful form of divine order , they received its stamp . They copied it in likeness at every successive degree of descent — and what they copied was made into forms at each level , even down to the lowest and most fixed natural tru ths, the very foundations of the mind — from state to state. The form of divine order that was displayed in the natural world left its im press and its stamp throughout all degrees of existence , being received and revealed at every level.

---

** ¶11.** Now, the new formation that was brought forth in this new manner in the world — the natural will and natural understanding — is unlike anything that had existed in those lower states of mind since the beginning. No such form had ever appeared in the lower degrees , because the image of divine order had never before descended to those depths.

---

**¶12.** Not all the forms that have been fashioned in the mind were fashioned through the open conjunction of higher wisdom with lower reception . Rather , there are other forms that arose by different means.

---

**¶ 13.** The first of these is a monstrous falsity dwelling in the sensory mind — a swe eping dist urb ance cast from the outermost boundary of heaven by the Divine source of all life into the aggregate of natural knowledge. Its own self-love and its own perverted reasoning shaped it into a distinct and terrible form.

---

**¶ 14.** The second form is one that fell into the natural mind and made the sensory level of knowledge its generative ground. Its own perv erted desire became its sculptor. By itself alone it fash ioned itself into a nature that is the root of spiritual death. And when it arose from the sensory level , it sought to destroy all the works of spiritual life. Immediately , the invincible power of Divine Truth — the great instruction of spiritual strength — was sent against it. It was subdued and hum bled in the ou termost states of obscurity and ignor ance. It is held underfoot and pressed down until the cons ummation of the age .

---

**¶15 .** The third form is a nature that fell upon the receptive ground of the natural mind itself . It fashioned itself into a fixed perception and established itself there — a new form generated not from above but from the ground of natural existence .

---

**¶16 .** In their essence , all these forms share in the nature of falsity and spiritual darkness . Yet they did not descend with the supreme ruling evil into the world. Rather, their fashioning came about subsequently — they are composite states , mix tures of truth and falsity, and they have been made manifest in the natural world as such .
